findings.title: Discard the pool when switching to the test database
findings.why_it_matters: If database access opens a pool before test database setup, the test runner changes the configured database name but continues using the pool connected to the original database. Migrations and tests can then run against the original database, including destructive test operations. Closing and removing the pool before changing database names ensures subsequent connections target the test database.
findings.suggested_fix: Close and remove the PostgreSQL pool when create_test_db switches the database name, and also when restoring the original name on teardown including keepdb; add a regression test that opens the pool before setup.
evidence: django/db/backends/base/creation.py:64-66 closes only the wrapper connection and changes NAME before migrate; the alias-keyed pool retains its original connection parameters.
django/test/runner.py:1054-1061 builds the test suite before setting up test databases.

findings.title: Enable pooling for an empty options dictionary
findings.why_it_matters: Configuring OPTIONS['pool'] as an empty dictionary silently disables pooling, although the documented dictionary form should use the connection pool defaults. Deployments using this valid configuration instead open a new database connection for each request and lose the expected connection limit and reuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish an absent or explicitly false pool option from an empty dictionary, and exercise the empty dictionary configuration in a pooling test.
evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:205 -- if self.alias == NO_DB_ALIAS or not pool_options:
docs/ref/databases.txt:255-258 documents a dictionary passed to ConnectionPool and True for defaults.
